newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stock rise sharply on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stock rise sharply on foreign buying.

text.p: Jordanian shares rallied at the start of weekly trade on Saturday, lifted higher after a buying spree by foreign funds in industrial blue-chips, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index jumped 1.60 percent to 156.64 points, its highest level since the end of February, after trade worth 1,149,714 dinars ($1.6 million).
But heightened investor confidence fuelled the select purchases by outside funds on industrial and mining firms such as Jordan Phosphates and Jordan Cement and Arab Potash APOT.AM.

This also helped pull along local investors who have been absent lately and awaiting a prod to reactivate purchases in many blue-chips which have become attractive after recent price falls, brokers said.

The bourse is also basking in a wave of optimism after the government passed two key investment reform laws last week which were applauded by investors as new evidence the government was serious in accelerating moves to open the economy to foreigners.
Dealers said foreign investors also appeared to have taken their cue from an investor road show in London last week to promote emerging fund investment in Jordanian blue-ships.
Among the busiest performers on Saturday were Jordan Cement, Arab Potash and Jordan Phosphate, all major producers and export earners for the kingdom.
They rose 0.05 dinars to 3.80 dinars, 0.23 dinars to 6.33 dinars and 0.10 dinars to 3.43 dinars respectively.
A three dinar rise in Arab Bank to 262.000 dinars was mainly sparked by the passage into law on Saturday of an overhauled companies statute, brokers said.

Arab Bank along with other banks had promised shareholders a bonus share once the government passes the law which cancels a 15 percent tax on companies raising their capital bases by transferring money from reserves.
Overall rising stocks outnumbered falling stocks by 28 to 13, with another six trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.79 percent to 80.39 points, still 0.79 percent down from the start of the year.
